purpose: Published contextual comparisons for transcript segmentation and downstream language metrics. None is a common-data head-to-head result or universal human error floor.

sources.citation: Liu, MacWhinney, Fromm & Lanzi (2023). Automation of Language Sample Analysis.
sources.population_input: Adult Delaware MCI/control speech; Batchalign first-pass output compared with human-corrected transcripts
sources.comparison_limit: Different population, available context and scoring. Preserve table/prose discrepancy. Local checkpoint adapter is not the full published system.

sources.citation: Pelfrey, Justice, Gonzalez Villasanti & Foster (2024). Evaluating the accuracy of automated processing of child and adult language production in preschool classrooms.
sources.population_input: Preschool classroom speech; manual timestamps, Whisper ASR, MATLAB language measures
sources.measure: median absolute relative error over six-minute segments; MLU is words/utterances
sources.comparison_limit: Includes transcription error; aggregation and linguistic eligibility differ from our fixed-word paragraph experiment. MLU definition must be stated when comparing.

sources.citation: Maltman, Hilvert, Friedman & Sterling (2023). Comparison of Linguistic Error Production in Conversational Language Among Boys With Fragile X Syndrome + Autism Spectrum Disorder and Autistic Boys.
sources.population_input: 11 independently retranscribed conversational SALT samples (28.21% of clinical samples)
sources.derivation: 100 minus reported agreement; no claim of independently known true human errors
sources.comparison_limit: Agreement is not boundary F1; disagreement is not MLU percentage error; word-identification agreement is not WER. Consensus resolved disagreements.

sources.citation: MacFarlane et al. (2023). Consistency and reliability of automated language measures across expressive language samples in autism.
sources.population_input: Autistic verbally fluent participants ages 6-23; SALT C-unit transcription
sources.comparison_limit: Audio-informed human C-units and percent agreement differ from text-only CHAT word-gap F1; not a human performance ceiling.

sources.citation: Wilder & Redmond (2022). The Reliability of Short Conversational Language Sample Measures in Children With and Without Developmental Language Disorder.
sources.population_input: 10 independently retranscribed conversational samples, five typical-language and five DLD
sources.measure: average-measures consistency ICC, two-way random effects
sources.comparison_limit: Morpheme-based MLU, not MLUw. Consistency ICC is not absolute agreement or percentage error; 1 minus ICC is not human error rate.

sources.citation: Xiong et al. (2016, revised February 2017). Achieving Human Parity in Conversational Speech Recognition.
sources.population_input: Professional transcribers, adult NIST 2000 telephone speech
sources.comparison_limit: Actual WER, but adult telephone speech only. Not a child/autism norm, segmentation result or downstream metric error. Current project round defers audio evaluation.
